title: Quantitative density gradient analysis of human mitochondrial ribosome by mass spectrometry
author: Páleníková, Minczuk, et al.
materials: This section describes analysis of peptide level data with the use of ComPrAn R package. As an output, a table of normalized protein data, lists of proteins detected only in one sample, a table of clustered proteins, as well as various visualizations of results are created. Analysis steps are illustrated in Methods Video S1.Note: Two types of input data can be used in ComPrAn: i) peptide data or ii) normalized protein data. In this protocol steps 51 to 58 describe a workflow for processing peptide level data, that results in the generation of normalized protein data which are used from step 59 onwards.Note: ComPrAn contains internal example datasets: i) peptide dataset obtained with Proteome Discoverer version 1.4 (Thermo Fisher Scientific) in combination with Mascot database for peptide quantification and identification, respectively and ii) normalized protein dataset obtained by processing the example peptide dataset (i) in ComPrAn. These datasets can be accessed, and the first 6 rows viewed by entering following code in R:# load ComPrAn packagelibrary(ComPrAn)# locate peptide datasetinputFile <- system.file("extData", "data.txt", package = "ComPrAn")# read in example peptide dataset using the designated# ComPrAn import functionpeptides <- peptideImport(inputFile)# locate normalised protein datasetinputFileProtein <- system.file("extData", "dataNormProts.txt",package = "ComPrAn")# read in file using the dedicated ComPrAn function, this# function automatically changes the structure of the table to# the required formatproteins <- protImportForAnalysis(inputFileProtein)# display first 6 rows of peptides datahead(peptides)# display first 6 rows of protein datahead(proteins)50.Start R, load the ComPrAn package and launch the Shiny app by entering the following code.# load ComPrAn R packagelibrary(ComPrAn)# launch the Shiny appcompranApp()51.Import the data by clicking on ‘Import’ tab and ‘Browse…’ button; navigate to the file produced in step 48 and click Open.52.After progress bar shows “Upload complete” click ‘Process data’ button.53.Specify names of the labeled (“heavy”) and unlabeled (“light”) samples in the appropriate boxes (these names will be used in plots later).54.Switch to the ‘Peptide-to-protein’ tab and click on ‘Summary’ section in the list that will appear.Note: Summary plots contain the information about total number of peptides and number of peptides in the two studied samples that passed the initial filtering (removes peptides which were not assigned into a protein group, had missing precursor area value or had a “Rejected” value of PSM (peptide spectrum match) ambiguity).55.Switch to the ‘Filter and Select’ tab. Adjust the available setting and click ‘Filter the data’ button. Plots summarizing total number of proteins in samples are shown.56.In the same tab, click ‘Select peptides’ button to select representative peptides that will represent each protein in the following analysis.57.Switch to ‘Rep Peptides’ tab.Note: On this page all peptides for any given protein can be visualized with the option to highlight the peptide that was selected by the analysis software as representative of the protein. Additionally, lists of proteins that were detected in both or only one of the two samples can be downloaded.58.Switch to ‘Normalize’ tab. Click on ‘Normalize the data’ button; all protein quantity values will be normalized to be between 0 and 1, a progress bar will appear in the bottom right corner, indicating processing of the data, once finished a message “Part 1 analysis finished, you may proceed to Part 2” will be shown.Pause point: normalized data can be exported in tab delimited format and used as alternative input to continue with analysis straight from step 59.59.Switch to ‘Protein workflow’ and click on ‘Normalized Proteins’ tab in the list that will appear. A protein can be selected from drop down menu for visualization of its quantitative comparison between labeled and unlabeled samples (Figures 5).Note: Each section of ‘Protein workflow’ provides a visualization option for the protein-level data to compare proteins and protein complexes quantitatively or qualitatively. Multiple options for customization of plots are provided, and each plot can be exported as a pdf file.60.Switch to ‘Heatmap’ tab, click on ‘Browse…’ and navigate to the file with information about the protein complex of interest. This produces a heatmap showing the quantitative comparison of protein profiles between samples (Figures 5).61.Switch to ‘Co-migration plots’ tab, paste UniProt IDs of interest in a box to qualitatively compare the profile of one or two protein complexes.62.Switch to ‘Cluster’ tab. This section provides functionality for clustering analysis. Proteins are assigned into clusters, separately for each sample, based on correlation of protein migration profiles. Plots showing the number of proteins per cluster and table with proteins assigned into clusters can be downloaded.Alternatives: The analysis described here with the use of ComPrAn app can also be performed directly from the R command line with the use of ComPrAn functions. For step-by-step guidelines use ComPrAn R package vignettes that can be accessed by entering following commands into R: This will open a web page with a list of available vignettes. Command line analysis of peptide-level data is described in a “SILAC complexomics” vignette and analysis of protein-level data is described in “Protein workflow” vignette.browseVignettes("ComPrAn")

steps.title: Culture control and test cells
steps.instruction: Grow the control (c) and test (t) HEK‑293 (or other) cells in their regular culture medium until they are fully adapted; if cells were thawed, passage them a few times before starting. This step may take 1–7 days.

steps.title: Prepare light and heavy SILAC media
steps.instruction: Make light (L) and heavy (H) SILAC media using pre‑warmed reagents and filter‑sterilize them.

substeps.instruction: Pre‑warm two 500 mL bottles of DMEM for SILAC and two 50 mL vials of dialyzed fetal bovine serum (dialyzed with 10 000 MW cutoff against 0.15 M NaCl until glucose < 5 mg/dL) in a 37 °C water bath.

Thaw or prepare fresh two 5 mL vials of penicillin‑streptomycin, a 500 µL aliquot of light arginine, heavy arginine, light lysine, heavy lysine, and two aliquots of proline; allow frozen aliquots to reach room temperature (18 °C–25 °C).
Place the warmed solutions and two filtering units inside a laminar‑flow hood.

In the cup of a filtering unit, prepare light medium (L) by adding 500 mL DMEM for SILAC, 50 mL dialyzed FBS, 5 mL penicillin‑streptomycin, 500 µL L‑proline, 500 µL light L‑arginine, and 500 µL light L‑lysine.

In a second filtering unit, prepare heavy medium (H) by adding 500 mL DMEM for SILAC, 50 mL dialyzed FBS, 5 mL penicillin‑streptomycin, 500 µL L‑proline, 500 µL heavy L‑arginine, and 500 µL heavy L‑lysine.

Connect each filtering unit to the low‑pressure line and filter‑sterilize the contents into the corresponding bottle. After sterilization, disconnect the line, disassemble the unit, and cap the bottle. Store filter‑sterilized SILAC media at 4 °C for up to 6 months.

steps.title: Install R and ComPrAn package
steps.instruction: Set up the computational environment required for data analysis.

substeps.instruction: Install R from https://www.r-project.org/ (if not already installed).
In an R session, run:
if (!requireNamespace("BiocManager", quietly = TRUE)) install.packages("BiocManager")
BiocManager::install("ComPrAn")

steps.title: Process raw MS data with Proteome Discoverer
steps.instruction: Identify and quantify peptides from the raw mass‑spectrometry files.

substeps.instruction: Open the Proteome Discoverer Daemon Utility and submit the raw files for all fractions.

Identify peptides by searching MS/MS spectra against the appropriate Mascot database (e.g., human UniProt) with the following parameters: precursor mass tolerance 10 ppm, fragment mass tolerance 0.5 Da, trypsin protease, one missed cleavage allowed, dynamic modifications – N‑terminal acetylation, formylation, oxidation of methionine, propionamide on cysteine, and heavy‑labelled lysine and arginine.
Quantify the identified peptides.
Open the report that contains all fractions.
Export the report as a single tab‑delimited text file, ensuring the “Peptides” box is checked; the filename will automatically receive the stem “psms”.
Use this exported file as input for the ComPrAn R package.

steps.title: Launch ComPrAn app and import data
steps.instruction: Start the interactive ComPrAn Shiny application and load the peptide report.

substeps.instruction: Start R, load the package with library(ComPrAn), and launch the app via compranApp().
In the app, click the ‘Import’ tab, press ‘Browse…’, navigate to the “psms” file produced in the previous step, and click Open.
When the progress bar shows “Upload complete”, click the ‘Process data’ button.
Enter the sample names for the labeled (“heavy”) and unlabeled (“light”) conditions in the appropriate boxes.

steps.title: Filter, select, and normalize peptide data
steps.instruction: Perform quality filtering, representative‑peptide selection, and data normalization within ComPrAn.

substeps.instruction: Switch to the ‘Peptide‑to‑protein’ tab and open the ‘Summary’ section to view total peptide counts and filtering statistics.
Go to the ‘Filter and Select’ tab, adjust settings as desired, and click ‘Filter the data’; summary plots of protein numbers will appear.
In the same tab, click ‘Select peptides’ to choose representative peptides for each protein.
Open the ‘Rep Peptides’ tab to visualise all peptides for any protein and optionally download lists of proteins detected in one or both samples.
Navigate to the ‘Normalize’ tab and click ‘Normalize the data’; a progress bar will run and, upon completion, the message “Part 1 analysis finished, you may proceed to Part 2” will appear.
Pause point – you may export the normalized data as a tab‑delimited file for later use.

steps.title: Analyze protein‑level data and visualizations
steps.instruction: Explore normalized protein data, generate plots, and perform clustering using ComPrAn.

substeps.instruction: Enter the ‘Protein workflow’ section and open the ‘Normalized Proteins’ tab; select a protein from the drop‑down menu to view its quantitative comparison between heavy and light samples.
Go to the ‘Heatmap’ tab, click ‘Browse…’, and load a file containing information about the protein complex of interest to produce a heatmap of quantitative profiles.
Open the ‘Co‑migration plots’ tab, paste UniProt IDs of interest, and generate qualitative co‑migration plots for one or two complexes.
Switch to the ‘Cluster’ tab, run the clustering analysis to assign proteins into correlation‑based clusters for each sample, and download the resulting plots and tables.
Optional: perform the same analyses from the R command line using the ComPrAn vignettes (browseVignettes("ComPrAn")).
